aiOverview.content: The Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) is a senior-level U.S. agency established in 2004 to oversee, integrate, and coordinate the 18 elements of the Intelligence Community (IC). Led by the Director of National Intelligence (DNI), it ensures timely, objective intelligence to national leaders and manages the National Intelligence Program.Core Functions and ResponsibilitiesIntelligence Integration: Leads the IC to produce unified intelligence, particularly through national centers focused on counterterrorism, counterintelligence, and cyber threats.Budget Authority: Develops and oversees the annual budget for the National Intelligence Program.Principal Advisor: The DNI acts as the primary intelligence advisor to the President, the National Security Council, and the Homeland Security Council.Information Sharing: Promotes sharing among intelligence agencies while protecting sources and methods.Partnerships: Engages with the private sector to acquire cutting-edge technology and expertise.Key ComponentsNational Counterterrorism Center (NCTC)National Counterintelligence and Security Center (NCSC)National Counterproliferation and Biosecurity Center (NCBC)Cyber Threat Intelligence Integration Center (CTIIC)Foreign Malign Influence Center (FMIC)The ODNI was created following the 9/11 attacks to prevent intelligence failures by ensuring better coordination among agencies. It is headquartered in McLean, Virginia.
